title: Default, Cure and Recovery of Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease Units
content:
# Default, Cure and Recovery — Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease

**Default.** A unit schedule may be declared in default only when its days past due are at least the tier's default threshold in days. The days past due are read from the unit's own record.

**Cure.** A default is cured only when every past-due invoice on the master agreement is paid, since curing a default requires every past-due invoice on the master agreement to be paid. The test reads the charges due of every unit under that master agreement, not only the unit in default.

**Recovery.** An uncured default leads to recovery of the unit, which is billed the recovery fee, then sold and settled under the terminal rental adjustment rule.

## Judgement table

| Situation | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Days past due below the tier's threshold | default may not be declared |
| Days past due equal to the threshold | default may be declared |
| Days past due above the threshold | default may be declared |
| The unit in default paid up, another unit of the same master agreement still past due | not cured |
| Every past-due invoice on the master agreement paid | cured; the schedule resumes |
| Default not cured | the unit is recovered and billed the recovery fee, then sold and settled under the terminal rental adjustment rule |

## Boundary illustration (hypothetical, threshold of 60 days)

At 59 days past due the unit schedule of the Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease may not be declared in default; at 60 days it may.
